title: Ads in AI Mode expand to new markets.
claims: Google announced that ads in AI Mode are scaling to Australia, Canada, India, Kenya, Malaysia, New Zealand, Nigeria, Pakistan, the Philippines and Singapore.
Google plans to expand to Brazil, Mexico and the United Kingdom during Q4 2026.
Multi-turn ads are launching in the United States, and ads are to be labeled Sponsored.
Google says AI Mode queries are on average three times longer than traditional searches.
limitations: Google's statement on click-through-rate similarity relies on Google internal US data from August 20 to September 3, 2026.
The post does not establish availability in all countries or performance outside the United States.
Brazil, Mexico and the United Kingdom are planned Q4 expansions rather than confirmed deployments as of the source date.

title: Google expands AI Search ads globally as core ad growth slows
claims: TechCrunch reports that Google announced international expansion of ads in AI-powered Search experiences during Alphabet's third-quarter earnings call.
The article reports Google's launch of multi-turn ads and AI Mode in the United States.
The article attributes the expansion and claimed early format results to Alphabet's earnings call and Google executives.
limitations: The article reports company statements; it does not independently measure campaign performance.
The article does not provide country-by-country operational availability details beyond the company's announcement.

title: Pinterest unlocks premium inventory for programmatic buyers, scaling high-intent discovery
claims: Pinterest announced general availability of Programmatic Deals in select global markets.
The announcement states current availability in North America, South America and Asia Pacific.
Programmatic Deals offer selected Pinterest display and video inventory through programmatic buying workflows.
Pinterest names Magnite as its primary supply-side partner and lists Amazon Ads DVA+, Google Display & Video 360, Yahoo DSP and DeepIntent among demand-side platforms.
limitations: The source is a Pinterest supplier announcement, not independent performance research.
The publication does not list all eligible countries, pricing or contractual requirements.
Its Moroccanoil example is a June 2026 campaign using Amazon internal data and is explicitly described as not indicative of future performance; it is not retained as a case study.
